c.tagline: Sardinia's sun-baked capital: hilltop Castello, Roman ruins, and Poetto beach.

taxi.fareNote: Uber does not operate in Cagliari or Sardinia; use the official white metered taxis at ranks, or phone/app-book a radio taxi (Radiotaxi 4 Mori and Rossoblu). Fares are metered with supplements for luggage and night rides.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

hood_landmark.Castello: Castello district Cagliari Bastione Saint Remy

avoid.reason: Minor bag and beach-belonging theft around the Marina district, the station and Poetto beach in summer.

hood_desc: Cagliari's oldest quarter, a walled citadel on the hill wrapped in medieval towers, the cathedral and the Bastione di Saint Remy terraces; steep, atmospheric streets with the best views, ideal for sightseeing (mind the stairs and few elevators).

The flat, lively grid between the Castello hill and the port, packed with restaurants, wine bars and shops along Via Roma; the easiest first-time base with great transport links, though it can be noisy at night.
The prettiest of the old quarters, a residential neighborhood of pastel houses, artisan workshops and the Basilica of San Saturnino; quieter and lived-in, a short walk east of the center.
The most authentic working old quarter, home to the Roman amphitheatre, the botanical gardens and everyday markets; central and walkable but calm at night, a good local base.

Cagliari's famous beach district, a long white-sand strip backed by lidos, kiosks and cycle paths along the Marina Piccola and the Molentargius salt flats with their flamingos; a relaxed, sun-and-sea base a bus ride from the center.

water.note: Tap water is safe, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: CTM buses run roughly 5:30am to around midnight, with a limited late-night 'Linea Notte' on weekends; the Metrocagliari light rail runs daytime into mid-evening.
transit.note: Getting around blends CTM's dense city bus network with the two-line Metrocagliari light rail (ARST) that runs north from Piazza Repubblica to the suburbs; the historic center is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Buy CTM tickets (about €1.30 for 90 minutes) at tobacconists, machines or the CTM/DropTicket app before boarding, and validate on board; you can also tap a contactless bank card on many buses. The Metrocagliari light rail uses the same integrated tickets.

ferry: Port of Cagliari (Via Roma cruise & ferry terminal)

transit.m: Trenitalia train to Cagliari Centrale (~7 min)
CTM/ARST bus to city center (~15 min)

tip.r: A service or cover charge (coperto) is often on the bill; rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is enough.
